sentence: Mashallah and [inshallah](/inshallah-meaning/) contain the same verb, shāʾa.
note: Target parses in shāʾa llāh using shāʾa; shared verb only.
target_quote: 'Inshallah is built from three separate Arabic words, not one. إن (in) is a conditional particle meaning "if." شاء (shāʾa) is a past-tense verb meaning "he willed" or "he wished." الله (Allāh) is simply the Arabic word for God, used by Arabic-speaking Muslims, Christians, and Jews alike. Strung together, in shāʾa Allāh reads literally as "if God has willed [it]," which English renderings soften to "God willing" or "if God wills." Wiktionary\'s entry for the phrase preserves exactly this three-part structure rather than treating it as a single fused word. The related phrase [mashallah](/mashallah-meaning/) is built on the same verb but means "God has willed it," not "God willing."',
